description.en: The aim of the experiment is to verify Norton’s Theorem.
The Instructions provide step-by-step guidance on how to perform the simulation.
The AI guide will assist you in performing the simulation accurately at each step.

The CHECK button verifies all the connections to ensure that they are correct.
Note: (a) If a wire is connected incorrectly, click the corresponding label number to remove the connection.
(b) Sources should be switched ON only after the current case connections are verified.
The AUTO CONNECT button makes all the connections automatically.
The ADD button adds the readings to the observation table.

The CALCULATE button auto-fills the resistance and source values in the theoretical verification panel. For verification, you have to manually calculate the load current using the Norton theorem concept and verify it using the VERIFY button.
The RESET button refresh the simulation to its initial state for a fresh start.
The PRINT button allows you to print the simulation.
Set the values of R1, R2, R3 and RL by moving the resistance sliders. These resistance values will remain constant throughout the experiment to ensure accurate verification of Norton’s Theorem.

The digital multimeter is used in resistance (Ω) mode to measure the Norton equivalent resistance (RN​) across the load terminals after removing the load resistance and deactivating the independent voltage source (by replacing it with a short circuit), the equivalent resistance across the load terminals is measured.

This ammeter measures the Norton current (IN) and load current (IL) flowing through the load resistance (RL​). The measured load current is used to verify Norton's Theorem by comparing it with the theoretically calculated load current.

Rating: 0-10 A DC.

This section provides the required DC voltage to the circuit. The display shows the active voltage supplied to the circuit, and the slider can be used to set the desired voltage value. 

Rating: 15 V DC.
This section displays the circuit and allows users to make the required connections by dragging and dropping wires between the connection terminals.
This table records the measured Norton current (IN), Norton resistance (RN​), Load resistance (RL) and Load current (IL).
This section displays the equations used to determine the Norton equivalent resistance (RN), Norton current (IN) and Load current (IL).

This is the theoretical verification panel where Norton’s Theorem will be verified. Enter the required values and compare the calculated load current with the measured load current to verify the theorem.

The Report button generates a summarised report of the simulation. After completing the observation table and theoretical verification, generate the report. The report will include the time taken to complete the simulation, no. of attempts, simulation summary, the apparatus used, recorded readings, the user-calculated result and the conclusion.
